newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks set for another record day.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks set for another record day.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to drive deeper into record ground on Thursday, buoyed by an overnight drop in the U.S. long bond yield which spurred a record-breaking rally in Wall Street stocks.

"Wall Street continued to break record highs and the long bond yield continued to fall and that will be positive for interest rate sensitive stocks," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
He expected the Hang Seng Index to gain 100 to 200 points, propelled higher by property and banking stocks. The index rose 211.12 points to a record close of 15,983.18 on Wednesday.
Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London surged another 117.82 points, or 0.74 percent, to 16,101.00.
The Dow industrials gained 80.36 points to a record close of 8,254.89 overnight as the U.S. long bond yield slipped to 6.33 percent, its lowest level since February 16, 1996.
"The market should hold up well on the back of what Wall Street did," said Kent Rossiter at Nikko Securities.
Brokers said after hefty gains this week, stocks could run into some profit-taking after early gains.
